doc:
Biology 2022 Ordinary Level, deferred sitting: reviewed task ledger, carded for the first time.

Independent visual sweep (2026-11-19), every page rendered and read:
  * LC025GLP038EV (deferredexams/2022; Sections A and B and Answerbook), 40 pages: p1 cover, p2
    instructions, p3-p6 Section A Questions 1-7, p7-p9 Section B Questions 8-10, p10 Section C
    answerbook instructions, p11-p12 graph paper, p13-p39 ruled answer pages, p40 back cover with the
    copyright notice.
  * LC025GLP040EV (Section C), 12 pages: p1 cover, p2-p10 Questions 11-17, p11 "Do not hand this
    question paper up", p12 back cover with the copyright notice.
  * LC025GLP000EV (deferredmarkingschemes/2022), 24 pages: p1 cover, p2 the deferred-scheme note, p3
    introduction, p4-p5 marking examples, p6-p22 Questions 1-17, p23 blank, p24 back cover.

The sitting has the June 2022 Ordinary shape (any four of Section A, any one of B, any three of C). The
deferred scheme sets out every printed ask, so no card needs the "prints no answer" row. Tariffs as the
scheme prints them: Q1, Q3 and Q7 five answers at 4; Q2, Q4, Q5 and Q6 one ladder each, 6(3) + 2;
Section B parts (a) 2(3) and (b) 8(3); Section C ladders 5 + 2(2), 3(5) + 6(2) and 2(6) + 6(2) under
each part's "Number of correct responses" table; Q16 and Q17 any two of (a)-(d), each 2(7) + 8(2).
Every response on a ladder is carded at the ladder's first rate, and each part's responses are counted
against its table (CHECKSUMS). Two definitions are set over two printed lines that the tables count as
two responses: Q17(c)(i) excretion and Q17(d)(i) evolution, the only count that reaches each table's
ten. Q6's ticks are read from their positions (Wingdings 2 check marks). Numbered asks (Q11(b)(i)1-4,
Q12(b)(i)1-3, Q12(c)(iii)1-5, Q15(c)(iv)1-2, Q16(a)(ii)1-2, Q16(b)(vi)1-2, Q16(c)(i)1-2,
Q17(b)(ii)1-3, Q17(c)(ii)1-2, Q17(c)(vi)1-2) are separately counted responses, carded one each. Three
answers are printed at the end of their reprint's line (Q12(b)(i)2 "Nn", Q12(c)(iii)1 "XY", Q17(b)(ii)3
"Correct location indicated") and are read from there. The scheme's completed Punnett square for
Q12(b)(ii) is that card's solution figure.
SELECTION_SCAN: Instructions: "blue or black pen", not a question.
Section A rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section B rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section C rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Q2(a) "Complete the following": every item asked, one card each.
Q3 "Complete the following sentences": every sentence asked.
Q5(a) "Complete the following": every item asked, one card each.
Q6 "true or false": the answer options.
Q6(c) statement "one or more products": the statement judged, not a choice.
Q7 "Choose each structure": a matching list, every structure placed; one card per lettered function.
Q8(a) "each of the following terms": every term asked, one card each.
Q9(a)(i) "lipid or protein or carbohydrate": the answer options.
Q9(a)(ii) "folded or fibrous": the answer options.
Q10(b)(vi) "both the experiment and the control": both required; one card.
Section C rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Q11(b)(i) "each of the following": every process asked, one card each.
Q11(c)(iv) "any one of the following areas": open choice of area; one card.
Q12(a): every term asked, one card each.
Q12(b)(i): each genotype asked, one card per item.
Q12(b)(ii) "both heterozygous": the cross described, not a choice.
Q12(b)(ii) "Using a Punnett square, or otherwise": method, not a choice of task.
Q12(c)(iii): each cell asked, one card per item.
Q16 "any two of (a), (b), (c), (d)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q16(a)(ii) "the following shapes": each shape asked, one card per item.
Q16(c)(i) "each of the following": each source asked, one card per item.
Q16(c)(iv) "any one of the named products": open single answer; one card.
Q17 "any two of (a), (b), (c), (d)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q17(b)(i) "Label the following parts": every label asked; one card.
Q17(b)(ii) "the following events": each event asked, one card per item.
Q17(c)(iii) "found in both urine and sweat": the product described, not a choice.

q2-cell: Diagram of a plant cell: a rounded rectangle with a thick outer wall, a large dark round body, oval bodies with stacked internal lines, and a large clear central space; A points to two of the oval bodies, B to the outer wall, C to the dark round body and D to the clear central space.
q4-chain: The food chain as printed: A, an arrow, B, an arrow, C.
q5-male: Diagram of the human male reproductive system from the front: the bladder at the top, tubes looping from each testis up and over the bladder, a dark gland below the bladder, and the penis; A points to one of the looping tubes, B to a testis and C to the dark gland below the bladder.
q9-graph: Graph of rate of enzyme activity against temperature: the curve starts low and flat, then rises steeply; the rest of the axis is left empty for the student to complete.
q11-carbon: Diagram of part of the carbon cycle with five boxes: Carbon dioxide in air, Carbon in plants, Carbon in animals, Dead organic matter and Fossil fuels, joined by arrows labelled with letters: A and B between Carbon dioxide in air and Carbon in plants, C from Carbon in animals to Carbon dioxide in air, G from Carbon in plants to Carbon in animals, D from Carbon in plants and from Carbon in animals to Dead organic matter, E from Dead organic matter to Fossil fuels, and F from Fossil fuels to Carbon dioxide in air.
q12-cells: Diagram of two large cells, one containing XX and one containing XY, each with two arrows down to two smaller cells: the XX cell gives two cells each containing X, and the XY cell gives one cell containing X and one containing Y.
q12b-ii-scheme: The marking scheme’s answer: Nn x Nn; a Punnett square with N and N along the top and N and n down the side, the boxes reading NN, Nn, Nn and nn; then NN: Normal wing, Nn: Normal wing, nn: Short wing, beside the scheme’s five one-point notes.
q13-digestive: Diagram of part of the human digestive system: a large organ at the upper left labelled A, a small sac beneath it labelled B, a tube leading down from the top labelled D, a curved bag labelled E, and the start of the intestine curving below it labelled C.
q14-stem: Diagram of a section through a stem: a circle with small dark patches scattered through it; X points to one of the patches.
q14-plant: Drawing of a whole plant: A points to a flower at the top, B to the stem, C to the roots below the soil line, and a bracket labelled D spans everything above the soil.
q14-leaf: Diagram of a leaf cross section under a light microscope: E points to the top layer of cells, a bracket labelled F spans the cells in the middle of the leaf, and G and H point to two groups of cells in a bundle in the middle.
q15-heart: Diagram of the human heart in section: A points to the upper chamber on the left of the picture, B to the wall dividing the two sides, C to the lower chamber on the right of the picture, D to the upper chamber on the right of the picture, and X to a flap at the base of a large blood vessel leaving the top of the heart.
q16-viruses: Two virus particles: A is a round particle with a knobbly surface; B has a many-sided head on a long tail with thin legs at its base.
q16-mitosis: Diagram of a dividing cell: X-shaped chromosomes lined up across the middle of the cell, with lines fanning out from each end of the cell to them; Chromosome and Cell membrane are labelled, and X points to one of the lines.
q16-plant: Drawing of a plant in soil with arrows: Light coming in from above, Carbon dioxide going into the leaves and Oxygen coming out.
q16-arm: Drawing of the bones and muscles of a bent human arm: Biceps and Triceps are labelled; X points to the bone of the upper arm, and Y and Z to the two bones of the forearm.
q17-amoeba: Diagram of an Amoeba: an irregular cell with finger-like extensions; A points to a large round body near the middle, B to the outer edge of the cell, C to a small round body containing a dark particle, and a clear round space is labelled Contractile vacuole.
q17-graph: Graph of urine and sweat produced (cm3/hour, 0 to 200) against outside temperature (°C, 0 to 40): the Urine line falls steadily from 100, and the Sweat line stays low then rises steeply, crossing the Urine line partway along.
q13b-i-question: The printed question: (b) The photograph shows the mouth of a carnivore. This animal demonstrates heterotrophic nutrition, with carnivore and heterotrophic underlined, then (i) Explain the underlined terms.
q17d-i-question: The printed question: (d) The evolution of birds has occurred over 10 million years and has led to increased variation and the development of 10,000 species of birds on Earth today, with evolution and species underlined, then (i) Explain briefly the underlined terms.
q13-mouth: Photograph of the wide-open mouth of a carnivore, showing long pointed canine teeth at the front and the teeth behind them.
